issues.legal_issue: A notification preserved by a transition law may be treated as made under a corresponding provision of the replacement law despite differences in the procedures prescribed by the two laws.
material_facts: The former state law authorized the forest-area notifications without the elaborate preliminary procedure prescribed by the replacement law.

The replacement law was extended to the territory, the former law was repealed, and a saving proviso deemed actions taken under the former law to have been taken under corresponding provisions of the replacement law.
issues.conclusion: The absence of identical procedural requirements did not prevent the preserved notifications from being treated as notifications under a corresponding provision of the replacement law.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3 and 4 of the Part C States (Laws) Act, 1950, including the proviso to section 4, actions under a repealed corresponding law could be deemed to have been taken under the corresponding provision of the extended law. Whether a notification was under a corresponding provision depended on the provision to which it corresponded, not on whether the old law prescribed the same preliminary procedure. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: replacement_law_extended and former_law_repealed and saving_clause_preserves_actions and notification_validly_made_under_former_law

predicates.replacement_law_extended: A replacement law was extended to the territory governed by the former law.
predicates.former_law_repealed: The former law was repealed because it corresponded to the extended replacement law.
predicates.saving_clause_preserves_actions: The transition law preserved actions taken under the former law by deeming them taken under corresponding provisions of the replacement law.
predicates.notification_validly_made_under_former_l: A notification was validly issued under the former law.

issues.definition: When a replacement law is extended, the former law is repealed, a saving clause preserves prior actions, and a notification was validly issued under the former law, the notification is treated as made under a corresponding provision even if the procedures differed.

issues.legal_issue: A notification under a law directed to protecting specified tree species does not establish that the notified area is a reserved forest under a replacement law whose reserved-forest provisions govern the forest area as a whole.
material_facts: The former state law principally protected specified classes of trees, and its notifications fixed the boundaries of three forest areas.
The notifications permitted certain existing settled uses and forest-product activities within the areas.

The replacement law distinguished between provisions for reserved forests, which concerned the forest area as a whole, and provisions for protected forests, which protected particular trees or classes of trees.

The prosecutions were for acts that constituted offences only if committed in a reserved forest; the areas had not been declared reserved forests through the replacement law’s reserved-forest procedure.
issues.conclusion: The notifications corresponded to the replacement law’s protected-forest provisions, not its reserved-forest provisions. The areas therefore were not established as reserved forests for the offences charged, and the acquittals were upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3, 4, 6, 7, 9, 11 and 20 of Chapter II of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, provide for constitution of a reserved forest after the prescribed process, including the determination or extinction of private rights, and section 26 penalizes specified acts in a reserved forest. Sections 30 to 33 in Chapter IV concern protected forests and the protection of particular trees or classes of trees. The Tripura Forest Act, particularly sections 4, 5, 16 and 19, was directed principally to protecting specified trees, so its notifications corresponded to Chapter IV rather than Chapter II. Sections 3 and 4 of the Part C States (Laws) Act, 1950, including the saving proviso to section 4, preserved the notifications only as actions under the corresponding provisions. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: prosecution_for_reserved_forest_offense and area_notified_under_tree_protection_law and former_law_targets_specified_tree_species and replacement_law_distinguishes_area_reservation_from_tree_protection

predicates.prosecution_for_reserved_forest_offense: A person was prosecuted for conduct that is an offence only if committed in a reserved forest.
predicates.area_notified_under_tree_protection_law: An area was notified under a former law directed to forest protection.
predicates.former_law_targets_specified_tree_specie: The former law principally protected specified tree species rather than reserving the forest area as a whole.
predicates.replacement_law_distinguishes_area_reser: The replacement law has distinct regimes for reserving an entire forest area and protecting particular trees or classes of trees.

issues.definition: If a reserved-forest offence is prosecuted in an area notified under a law directed to specified tree species, and the replacement law distinguishes area-wide reservation from tree protection, that notification does not establish reserved-forest status.
